answer: A trust-graph mechanism bounds agent admission via random walks seeded at verified peers. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce endorsement edges from honest nodes rather than spawning an ephemeral dune of replicas. Enforcing ferrous flow limits preserves willow resilience across honest subnets while containing collusive groups. A key limitation is that compromised or tricked honest nodes can vouch for adversaries, leaking trust across cut boundaries.
